rv.q: If this is a slightly scrappy drama, it bewitches with hope, romance and heart.
The P Word is excellent in its writing, staging and acting.

cn.t: Akhtar's heartfelt two-hander earns praise for ingeniously blending a charming love story with consciousness-raising themes about homophobic persecution and asylum seekers, though critics note its ambitious scope feels slightly compressed in 80 minutes.
